evidence.statement: Accepted answers and explanations consistently match the supplied definitions of patches, embeddings, transformers, attention, and ViT processing.
Each item has a clearly marked answer, and multi-select items identify complete sets without overlapping defensible distractors.

Distractors are drawn from adjacent concepts such as tokens, embeddings, attention, image patches, segmentation, and object detection, making them credible while remaining distinguishable under the prompt.
Wrong options explicitly target realistic confusions between inputs and representations, language and visual processing, and attention versus embeddings.

The session begins with useful definitions and reaches application scenarios, but it repeatedly switches between language and vision concepts and returns to recall after application, such as the dimensions item after the language-capabilities scenario and the attention item after several later items.
The artifact uses multiple-choice, multi-select, fill-blank, and sentence-arrangement mechanics, though the final third contains several closely spaced selection-oriented items.
Prompt forms vary between definitions, reconstruction, completion, and scenarios, but several items use similar architecture-selection or action-selection wording.
The comments, support-message, catalog, smart-checkout, and contextual-word scenarios represent credible applied decisions tied to the concepts being tested.

Incorrect options generally include both an intrinsic consequence and an instructional distinction, but many correct explanations only restate the answer and do not provide a next-step application or contrast.

The Level 2 session uses foundational definitions followed by applied selection scenarios, matching the stated conceptual audience, although several remembering items remain quite basic for learners assumed to know deep-learning fundamentals.
Token, embedding, vector, attention, image patch, vision transformer, and semantic language model are used consistently across prompts, options, answers, rationales, and feedback.

The complete sequence is source-aligned, answerable, and varied, with credible scenarios and strong misconception feedback; its main learner-experience weakness is the non-linear alternation between language foundations and vision-bridge content.

largest_gap.summary: The ordered sequence interleaves language foundations with vision-transformer bridge material and revisits recall concepts after application items.

evidence.statement: The sequence moves from image patches to embeddings, language uses, dimensions, language architecture, more embedding practice, ViT processing, token terminology, attention, ViT application, and only then contextual-word application.

largest_gap.repair_instruction: Reorder the existing items into a progression of token and embedding foundations, attention and transformer context, language-use applications, and then the vision-transformer bridge; preserve each item payload, answer index, identity, and sequence integrity.

result.concise_summary: The artifact is strongly source-faithful and deterministic gates appear intact, with clear answers, credible distractors, and useful misconception feedback. The main actionable weakness is session ordering: language foundations, applications, and vision-bridge material are interleaved. Confidence is reduced because no approved references were supplied and validation feedback reported an evidence-path mismatch.
